data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The finite obstruction structures are exactly the locally stable mixed configurations in which the crossing edges form a matching: every vertex has at most one neighbor of the opposite color, so no vertex can flip. The prevalence of reachable obstructions scales like exp(\u0398(n)): the expected number of final matchings of size \u03b1n is exp(n f(\u03b1)) with f(\u03b1)>0 for \u03b1 in (0,1/2), while the consensus basin has probability exp(-\u0398(n)).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the initial coloring is biased so that one color has density above the threshold for 2-core percolation, consensus may occur with high probability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the graph is bipartite or has no short cycles, the final matching size may be o(n) and the limit may change.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If updates are synchronous or if vertices are chosen adversarially, the process may not be cut-decreasing and the conclusion fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Let H be the subgraph of crossing edges. A vertex is unstable exactly when its H-degree is 2 or 3. Flipping such a vertex toggles all three incident edges, reducing total cut size by 1 (degree 2) or 3 (degree 3). The asynchronous process is therefore a cut-decreasing random walk that stops precisely when H has maximum degree 1, i.e. is a matching. On a random 3-regular graph the initial H is a Bernoulli(1/2) subgraph with a giant 2-core; the random flip cascade removes cycles but leaves a linear-size matching, so the final state is a nonempty stable mixed configuration with high probability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
